children: ) shares are trading lower Monday afternoon as a broad sell-off in global crude oil benchmarks erases recent geopolitical risk premiums following the stabilization of Middle Eastern supply routes.
Occidental Petroleum shares are under pressure.

The primary headwind causing Monday’s drop stems from West Texas Intermediate crude pricing slipping to near $97.98 per barrel during early market hours. Investors are potentially actively discounting the geopolitical supply fears that spiked after Saturday’s Houthi missile and drone strikes near Riyadh, reacting to indicators showing Saudi export capacities quickly recovered and stabilized.

Because the enterprise operates with a highly concentrated upstream production profile heavily weighted toward the Permian Basin, this sudden benchmark decline structurally squeezes projected near-term free cash flow.

This revenue reduction is particularly impactful for the firm, as management heavily relies on elevated crude realizations to aggressively fund its corporate debt reduction targets following the recent integration of large-scale regional acquisitions.
Occidental Petroleum shares were down 2.89% at $57.15 at the time of publication on Monday,
